A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same BAPO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM evaluations on synthetic reasoning problems, hotel-review tasks and variable tracking, including accuracy and reasoning-token results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original evaluations and their reported outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 6 newly sketches a two-pass attention variant: g2 receives tokens selected by g1, enabling attention to neighboring tokens. This is a prospective model extension presented as future work; the BAPO and BAPO-CoT definitions underlying the results remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic problems, SPACE review tasks and RULER-inspired variable tracking. The new induction-head discussion does not introduce an evaluated task.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain GPT-4o/mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet/Haiku and Gemini 1.5 Pro/Flash, with o3 and Gemini 2.5 Flash in the reasoning experiments. Newly cited induction-head methods are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C.1 retain the same data-generation procedures, input-size settings, API model versions, temperature settings, JSON output constraints and 250-word soft CoT limit.

E4.justification: The CoT tests, model/input-size comparisons and Disjointness-versus-IntDisjointness representation analysis are retained. No new ablation or robustness experiment accompanies the proposed attention extension.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 100 i.i.d. instances with 95% t-test confidence intervals. The new checklist restates this as 100 runs without documenting additional repetitions, seeds or a different uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: The accuracy and reasoning-token plots in Figures 1, 3–5 and 9–13 are unchanged, including the appendix results. Their empirical findings are retained; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects Theorem 3's construction from k=1,...,m to k=0,...,m-1 and replaces the comparison of (a,d) with (c,b) by (a,b) with (c,b), ensuring identical suffixes. The theorem statements and bounds remain unchanged. A counting inconsistency remains: the old ones-count expression for ad is attached to ab.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same claims about bandwidth limitations, BAPO hardness, empirical agreement and CoT's computational power. The separate conclusion reiterates existing practical implications.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly identifies difficulty linking neighboring tokens as a limitation relevant to induction heads and discusses additional attention passes as a possible remedy. It also explicitly states that tokenization errors fall outside BAPO's scope, so BAPO-easy does not guarantee LLM success.

D1.justification: The new checklist reports code with documentation as supplementary material and states that the repository includes data-download and experiment-running instructions. Existing implementation details, model settings, costs and the repository link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Bietti et al. (2023), Olsson et al. (2022), and Sanford et al.'s induction-head paper (2024) to support Section 6's discussion. The broader positioning remains stable; other reference edits largely concern bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v4 expands Section 2's explanation of causal information flow, separates Discussion and Conclusions, adds focused discussion paragraphs and appends a NeurIPS checklist. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a document-wide NeurIPS format, changing typography, margins, the title/author block, figure scaling and placement, and prompt-table wrapping. All 13 figures remain, but appendix plots are redistributed across pages. Table 1's caption additionally summarizes the existing CoT bound.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the Majority proof's indexing and shared-suffix reasoning, clarifies the model explanation, and acknowledges specific applicability limits. These provide a limited gain in rigor and clarity despite the remaining counting inconsistency. The empirical evidence and central claims are unchanged.
